title: Completed scalar extension comparison commutes with shifts
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $E\subseteq L$ finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subseteq\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Y$ be a scheme, with small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}=\varprojlim_{j\geq1}(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^j)_Y$, $F=E,L$, for its completed coefficient sheaves [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], with the canonical map $R_E\to R_L$. Let $K\in D(R_E)$ be a derived $t$-complete complex of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-derived-complete]. Write $T_{L/E}K=K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ for the strict-tower integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] and
$$
 \chi_K:K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L\longrightarrow T_{L/E}K
$$
for the canonical quotient-map completion comparison of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. For every $m\in\mathbf Z$, this natural transformation commutes with cochain shift $[m]$.

More precisely, take a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], put $D(P)=\prod_{j\geq1}\operatorname{Res}^L_j(P\otimes_{R_E}(\mathcal O_L/v^j)_Y)$, and let $h_P=1-s_P$ where $s_P$ is induced by the quotient transitions. Here $\operatorname{Res}^L_j$ is restriction along $R_L\to(\mathcal O_L/v^j)_Y$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. In the reordered cone $C(P)=\operatorname{Cone}(h_P)[-1]$ with $C(P)^r=D(P)^r\oplus D(P)^{r-1}$ and differential $(x,y)\mapsto(dx,-dy-h_Px)$, let $c:P\otimes_{R_E}R_L\to D(P)$ be the quotient maps, so that $\chi_P(z)=(c(z),0)$. The map
$$
 \alpha_{m,P}:C(P[m])\xrightarrow{\sim}C(P)[m],\qquad (x,y)\longmapsto(x,(-1)^m y)
$$
is a natural chain isomorphism, compatible with the standard zero-shift and successive-shift identifications, and satisfies $\alpha_{m,P}\chi_{P[m]}=\chi_P[m]$ after identifying $(P[m])\otimes_{R_E}R_L=(P\otimes_{R_E}R_L)[m]$. This identity descends to the stated shift compatibility of $\chi_K$ in $D(R_L)$, independently of the K-flat resolution.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat flat-term resolution $P\to K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $P\otimes_{R_E}R_L$ represents the ordinary derived extension. By [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], the product-and-cone complex $C(P)$ in the statement represents $T_{L/E}K$. The explicit normalization in [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] represents $\chi_K$ by $z\mapsto(c_Pz,0)$, where $c_P$ is the family of quotient maps. Indeed each quotient map is a chain map and the transitions give $h_Pc_P=0$ strictly, so $d_{C(P)}(c_Pz,0)=(c_Pdz,0)$. These statements apply on the small pro-etale site of the given scheme; they require neither a noetherian hypothesis nor a boundedness hypothesis on $K$.

source.place: Final equivalence display; explicit completed scalar comparison needed for common-stage shift transport (agent argument).

proof.text: Write $\epsilon_m=(-1)^m$ for any integer $m$. The shift convention [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is $P[m]^r=P^{r+m}$ with differential $\epsilon_m d_P$. This is again a flat-term K-flat complex: for an acyclic complex $A$, the total tensor convention [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes P[m])\cong\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes P)[m]$ by multiplying the summand with $A$-degree $i$ by $\epsilon_m^i$; both differentials agree because $\epsilon_m^{i+1}=\epsilon_m\epsilon_m^i$. The target is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex], since shifting merely reindexes cohomology. Flatness of terms is unchanged by reindexing. Tensoring $P$ with a ring sheaf placed in degree zero commutes with shifting without a sign on tensors. Degreewise products and scalar restriction also merely reindex. Hence $D(P[m])=D(P)[m]$, $h_{P[m]}=h_P[m]$, and $c_{P[m]}=c_P[m]$ under these identifications.

source.place: Tag 011G, definition-shift-cochain; direct calculation with the signed total tensor of Definition 012Z.

proof.text:
Reorder $\operatorname{Cone}(h_P)[-1]^r=D(P)^{r-1}\oplus D(P)^r$ into $(x,y)\in D(P)^r\oplus D(P)^{r-1}$. The cone and shift conventions of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] give the stated differential $(dx,-dy-h_Px)$. In degree $r$ the source $C(P[m])$ therefore has differential $(x,y)\mapsto(\epsilon_m dx,-\epsilon_m dy-h_Px)$, whereas the target $C(P)[m]$ has differential $(x,y)\mapsto(\epsilon_m dx,-\epsilon_m dy-\epsilon_m h_Px)$. Applying $\alpha_{m,P}(x,y)=(x,\epsilon_m y)$ before or after the respective differentials gives in both cases
$$ (\epsilon_m dx,-dy-\epsilon_m h_Px). $$
The same coordinate formula in the reverse direction is its inverse, since $\epsilon_m^2=1$. It is $R_L$-linear. Thus it is a chain isomorphism for every integer $m$, including negative integers.

proof.text:
For a chain map $f:P\to P'$, let $D(f)$ be its product of quotient tensor maps. Each transition square commutes, so $D(f)h_P=h_{P'}D(f)$, and the induced map of the reordered cones is $(x,y)\mapsto(D(f)x,D(f)y)$. This commutes with $(x,y)\mapsto(x,\epsilon_m y)$, proving naturality of $\alpha_m$. Under the standard degree-reindexing identification $P[m][n]=P[m+n]$, the composite
$$C(P[m][n])\xrightarrow{\alpha_{n,P[m]}}C(P[m])[n]\xrightarrow{\alpha_{m,P}[n]}C(P)[m][n]$$
multiplies the second coordinate by $\epsilon_n\epsilon_m=\epsilon_{m+n}$ and leaves the first fixed. This is $\alpha_{m+n,P}$. For $m=0$ its two components are identities. These are precisely the successive-shift and zero-shift laws.

source.place: Tag 011G, definition-shift-cochain and following paragraph on zero and successive shifts; direct calculation on the two cone coordinates.

proof.text:
Use the zero second-coordinate formula for the comparison from [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. With the identifications of step 2, for every local section $z$ of $(P\otimes_{R_E}R_L)[m]$ one has
$$\alpha_{m,P}\chi_{P[m]}(z)=\alpha_{m,P}(c_P[m](z),0)=(c_P[m](z),0)=\chi_P[m](z).$$
This is an equality of chain maps of $R_L$-module sheaves. In particular it uses the specified comparison arising from the compatible quotient maps, rather than a choice of a morphism completing an abstract triangle.

source.place: Final equivalence display; the fixed quotient-map comparison and its signed shift square (agent calculation).

proof.text: Pass to derived categories. The resolving-class equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identifies localization of the homotopy category of flat-term K-flat $R_E$-complexes at quasi-isomorphisms with $D(R_E)$. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](1)-(2), the ordinary tensor model inverts those quasi-isomorphisms, with its canonical comparisons. By [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined](1)-(2), the strict cone model also inverts them and its comparisons are independent of the resolution. Naturality in step 4 holds after passing to homotopy classes, then also for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms: invert the two vertical isomorphisms in its naturality square. Thus $\alpha_m$, its inverse, and the identities in steps 4-5 descend along this equivalence. They are natural on $D(R_E)$ and agree under the canonical comparisons from any two resolutions. The first model's shift comparison is the degreewise tensor identification of step 2, and the second model's is the descended $\alpha_m$. Finally [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies the descended map $\chi_P$ with the specified $\chi_K$. Step 5 now gives its required shift square in $D(R_L)$, with the zero and successive-shift laws of step 4. The chain calculation did not need completeness; in particular it applies to all the derived-complete inputs in the statement.
